irac.issue: Whether the Central Government can cancel a licence for the manufacture of rectified spirit if the licencee has not taken delivery of the spirit within the specified time period.
irac.rule: The Central Government has the authority to cancel a licence if the conditions specified in the licence or the rules and regulations made under the Act are not complied with.
irac.application: The licencee, Harbhajan Singh Dhillon, had not taken delivery of the rectified spirit within the specified time period, which was a condition of the licence. The Supreme Court held that the Central Government's order cancelling the licence was valid.
irac.conclusion: The Central Government's order cancelling the licence was valid, and the licencee was not entitled to compensation.
